entries.name: Mixture density network
entries.definition: A neural conditional-density architecture whose input-dependent outputs parameterize the mixing weights and component distributions of a finite mixture over target variables.
entries.identity_notes: This is Bishop’s combined neural-network and mixture-density construction. It predicts a conditional distribution, not only a conditional mean, and does not require the output density to be unimodal. The report’s worked model uses a feed-forward network and isotropic Gaussian components; other component families or covariance parameterizations are choices within the broader construction. It is distinct from an unconditional fitted Gaussian mixture, a generic feed-forward classifier and a sparse mixture-of-experts large language model. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 349 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines respectively. All 3 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: the prior NADE-variant lead, RNADE source URL and previous review exclusion, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Seventeen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Exponentiation makes the scale positive for finite real outputs but does not bound it away from zero or prevent likelihood concentration as a component scale approaches zero. The report’s wording about avoiding zero-variance pathologies is interpreted with this mathematical qualification.

The report sometimes calls sigma a variance, but Equation (23) uses sigma as a standard deviation. Its displayed population Equation (40) omits the negative sign required by the preceding negative-log-likelihood objective; Equations (43) and (47) omit dimension factors if read as general isotropic multivariate scale and total variance formulas. Those printed formulas are not adopted as general identities.
A mixture’s global mode generally requires optimization. Selecting a component center by peak height or weight is an approximation under separation assumptions, not an exact general mode calculation.

A finite architecture and local optimization do not establish an arbitrary-accuracy fit, calibrated uncertainty, successful generalization or global optimality. The network models p(t|x), not p(x), unless an additional input model is provided.
No author implementation, later experimental pages or general approximation theorem was audited; finite curator calculations check only the displayed cases.

claims.statement: For input x, a neural network outputs parameters defining p(t|x)=sum_i alpha_i(x) phi_i(t|x). In the report’s c-dimensional isotropic Gaussian construction, softmax outputs give nonnegative mixing weights summing to one, direct outputs give component means, and exponentiated outputs give positive standard deviations sigma_i, with covariance sigma_i squared times the identity. The mixture can have dependent target coordinates even though coordinates are independent within each isotropic component. Minimize the sum of negative log mixture densities over input/target pairs. With responsibilities r_i=alpha_i phi_i/p(t|x), the output-logit derivative of one negative log likelihood is alpha_i-r_i; the mean derivative is r_i(mu_i-t)/sigma_i squared and the log-scale derivative is r_i(c-||t-mu_i|| squared/sigma_i squared). Backpropagate these derivatives through the network. Mixture weights are conditional component priors before observing t; responsibilities condition on both x and t. The conditional mean is the weighted mean of component centers and need not be a mode or a plausible branch of a multivalued inverse mapping.

entries.name: Real-valued neural autoregressive density estimator
entries.definition: A fully visible neural autoregressive density architecture for real-valued vectors that shares input-to-hidden parameters across ordered scalar conditional mixture-density models.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes Uria, Murray and Larochelle’s original RNADE family. It extends binary NADE by replacing Bernoulli outputs with real-valued mixture conditionals. Deterministic prefix features and NADE-style input sharing distinguish it from separate untied conditional networks and from a stochastic latent RBM. Mixture-of-Gaussians and mixture-of-Laplace outputs are reported variants, not identity aliases for every Gaussian or Laplace mixture. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 349 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. All 3 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: the prior NADE-variant lead, RNADE source URL and previous review exclusion, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Seventeen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five full native neighboring records were inspected. limitations: The variable ordering, conditional family, hidden capacity, component count and optimization restrict the fitted density. Exact density evaluation does not make arbitrary missing-variable posterior inference a forward pass or establish data-model agreement.

Linear scaling in dimensionality holds with fixed hidden and mixture sizes; it does not omit their cost. The final prefix update is unnecessary, consistent with the declared H by (D-1) input-weight matrix.

The supplement labels several log-density derivative formulas as derivatives of p rather than log p. Its Algorithm 2 also uses a log-shaped expression with a positive squared-residual term as if it were a component density in responsibilities, and has prefix/index ambiguities. A literal finite example produces invalid responsibilities. The curated mechanism follows the main-paper normalized densities and prefix equations; this is not a claim about author-code behavior.

The experimental standard-deviation gradient rescaling is not the raw likelihood gradient or Newton’s variance scaling. Exponential scales remain susceptible to approaching zero; regularization and model selection matter.
No performance ranking, convergence guarantee, exact posterior claim or full executable implementation validation is included.

claims.statement: For an ordered real-valued vector x, evaluate p(x)=product_d p(x_d|x_<d). Start a_1=c and update a_(d+1)=a_d+x_d W[:,d] when another conditional remains. At each position, a learned scalar rho_d rescales the shared prefix preactivation; sigmoid or rectified-linear units produce deterministic hidden features h_d. Separate position-specific output matrices map those features to scalar-mixture parameters. In RNADE-MoG, softmax gives component weights, linear outputs give means, and exponentials give positive standard deviations. Summing the normalized scalar Gaussian components gives each conditional density; multiplying the conditionals yields a normalized joint without a global partition-function estimate. Complete-vector log densities and their derivatives are directly evaluable; prefix recurrence and fixed hidden/component sizes give cost linear in the number of dimensions, with output work O(DHK). Ancestral generation samples each scalar from the mixture conditioned on previously generated values. The experimental mean-output gradient rescaling by component standard deviation is a training heuristic, separate from the exact log-density derivative. The paper also substitutes Laplace mixture conditionals.

entries.name: Document NADE
entries.definition: A neural autoregressive document model that predicts successive words from shared additive embeddings of the preceding words, using normalized word conditionals and a deterministic document representation.
entries.identity_notes: This is Larochelle and Lauly’s original Document NADE. The final construction uses binary-tree word probabilities, with a flat-softmax intermediate derivation. It is inspired by Replicated Softmax but is a separately normalized directed model with deterministic hidden features, not the same undirected latent-variable model. Its full-document representation is invariant to word permutation, while its unsymmetrized sequence probability need not be. Supervised and distributional-prior extensions require separate scope decisions. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 349 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines respectively. All 3 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: the prior NADE-variant lead, RNADE source URL and previous review exclusion, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Seventeen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Order invariance of the summed document representation does not imply exchangeability of the sequence likelihood. The symmetrized probability of each sequence differs from its count-vector probability by the number of distinct permutations; duplicate words change that number.

For a word whose tree path has length L, conditional output work is O(HL). The claimed logarithmic vocabulary scaling requires suitable tree depth or average depth; a full binary tree alone can have linear depth. The record does not assert a logarithmic worst case for every full tree.

The main paper’s text below Equation (11) retains vi=1 in the joint product although words are categorical. The curated likelihood uses the observed word and its branch path, consistent with Equations (9) and (11) and the supplement’s probability computation.

For Bernoulli tree training, the negative-log-likelihood derivative is the probability of the right branch minus the observed branch indicator. The supplement’s p(actual branch)-indicator notation must not be read literally as the probability of the observed left branch when that indicator is zero. No author implementation behavior is inferred.

The stated model is conditional on document length and does not supply a learned document-length distribution. Shared additive prefix features discard order within the observed prefix. Hidden topic features are deterministic representations, not posterior latent-topic probabilities.
No classification/retrieval advantage, semantic quality guarantee, exact symmetrized-mixture training gradient or implementation certification is asserted.

claims.statement: For a document of given length D, form h_i=sigmoid(c+sum_(k<i) W[:,v_k]); the same word embedding and output parameters are reused across positions, and the preactivation is updated by adding the newly observed word’s embedding. A flat softmax can normalize the next-word distribution. The paper’s final model replaces it with a binary tree whose leaves are vocabulary words: each internal node predicts the probability of taking its right branch, and a word probability is the product of its observed left/right branch probabilities. Multiply all observed-word conditionals to obtain a normalized probability over length-D sequences. Train by differentiating their negative log likelihood. After all words, h(v)=sigmoid(c+sum_i W[:,v_i]) is an order-invariant document representation; tanh is also tested. For count-vector input, the paper samples word occurrences without replacement to produce uniformly random distinct orderings and trains on those sequences. Its separate symmetrized sequence model averages probabilities over distinct permutations; training on sampled order log losses is a surrogate for that log mixture. A count-vector probability instead sums the unsymmetrized sequence probabilities over its distinct permutations.

claims.statement: Fix an ordering of D binary observations. For each position i compute h_i=sigmoid(c+W[:,<i] x_<i) and r_i=P(x_i=1|x_<i)=sigmoid(b_i+V[i,:] h_i). The original motivation ties V to the transpose of W, while the paper explicitly also learns separate output weights V; sharing W and c across positions is retained. The joint probability is the product over i of r_i raised to x_i times (1-r_i) raised to (1-x_i). Initialize the hidden preactivation accumulator a_1=c and update a_(i+1)=a_i+W[:,i] x_i after evaluating position i. This reuses prefix work and supports O(DH) evaluation for the original one-hidden-layer construction with H hidden units. Train by differentiating the exact average negative log joint probability. Generate by sampling each visible bit from its prefix conditional in order; no stochastic hidden-state inference or RBM partition function is needed for these operations.

native_neighbors.name: Order-agnostic NADE training
native_neighbors.definition: A stochastic training procedure that shares neural conditional parameters across variable orderings and estimates the order-averaged NADE log-likelihood objective using a sampled observed prefix and losses for all remaining variables.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is Uria, Murray and Larochelle’s order-agnostic training procedure, applicable to shallow or deep NADE and its real-valued extension. It is distinct from the original fixed-order NADE architecture, the existence of additional deterministic hidden layers alone, and an ensemble mixture evaluated after training. Parameter sharing across orderings does not assert that every ordering defines the same joint distribution. Seventeen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Shared parameters do not force order-specific joint distributions to agree. Choosing an ordering convenient for a conditioning query performs inference under that chosen member, not necessarily under another ordering or the ensemble mixture.

Conditioning an ensemble generally reweights its members by their evidence probabilities. Uniformly choosing a member after observing evidence does not automatically sample the ensemble posterior; a finite curator example checks this distinction.

The unbiased prefix estimator depends on the stated uniform ordering/prefix sampling and D/(D-d+1) weighting. Arbitrary masks, unweighted missing-output losses or nonuniform prefix sampling require a corresponding derivation.

The presence mask is additional input information, not a sequence-timestep skipping layer or a guarantee that missing-data mechanisms have been modeled. The paper distinguishes its missing-output loss from ordinary denoising-autoencoder reconstruction.

The training objective is an average of log probabilities rather than the log of an average probability. Ensemble density evaluation costs and deep full-joint evaluation differ from one stochastic training update; selecting a convenient model is not dimension-independent numerical inference.
No agreement of all conditionals with one joint distribution, universal performance gain, global optimization guarantee or complete implementation audit is asserted.

claims.statement: Treat a variable ordering o as uniformly distributed over permutations and minimize the mean over data and o of the negative log probability assigned by the corresponding autoregressive NADE. For a training example, sample an ordering and a prefix length d-1 uniformly from zero through D-1. Feed the observed prefix values to the shared neural conditional network, set unobserved input values to zero and append a binary mask identifying observed dimensions so that observed zeros remain distinguishable from missing inputs. Evaluate the conditional loss for each of the D-d+1 remaining variables under that same prefix, sum those losses and multiply by D/(D-d+1). The resulting loss and, under the differentiability conditions, its gradient estimate the order-averaged objective; one masked-prefix forward/backward computation serves all missing outputs. Additional deterministic hidden layers can be used, while full joint evaluation for a chosen ordering still requires all ordered conditionals. After training, a selected ordering defines one normalized autoregressive model. A separate ensemble averages the joint probabilities of selected orderings, and samples by selecting a member then generating from that member. This probability average is distinct from the order-average log-likelihood training objective.

native_neighbors.definition: A fully observed binary autoregressive probabilistic model whose conditional probability at each position is a logistic function of a bias and a weighted sum of preceding visible variables.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is the fully visible sigmoid model discussed by Larochelle and Murray, with no stochastic hidden variables. Frey and colleagues call their binary logistic special case a fully visible belief network; that local usage does not make all fully visible Bayesian networks synonyms of the sigmoid family. The record specializes the broader sigmoid-belief-network family and is distinct from NADE’s nonlinear deterministic hidden features and DARN’s stochastic latent architecture. limitations: The chain-rule factorization is general, but restricting each conditional to a logistic-linear function limits the distribution family. A given fixed-order conditional table with a nonzero logit interaction cannot be represented by that affine logit; this is not a claim about every alternative ordering or latent extension.

Exact complete-observation likelihood and forward generation do not provide arbitrary missing-variable posteriors for free. Conditioning on a suffix while earlier variables are unknown still requires inference or summation.

Changing the variable order changes the restricted model family and can affect fitting. The absence of stochastic latent variables is part of this specialization, not a property of all sigmoid belief networks.

The source’s FVBN label is interpreted within its binary logistic model setting. No assertion that every fully visible Bayesian model uses logistic factors, no universal performance ranking and no trained-model result is included.

Multiply the corresponding Bernoulli probabilities over positions to evaluate the normalized observed joint. All variables in that product are visible, so complete-data likelihood evaluation has no hidden-state marginalization or recognition-model posterior approximation. Its negative log likelihood is the sum of the positionwise binary logistic losses. Generate a sample by drawing each bit from the conditional determined by already drawn predecessors. Full connectivity makes all earlier visible variables available as parents; zero coefficients can remove particular dependencies. A fixed-order conditional’s log odds are affine in its predecessors, unlike the more general nonlinear neural conditional used by NADE.

claims.statement: In the decoder, factor the top hidden prior along a fixed within-layer order. Each lower stochastic layer conditions each unit on the preceding units in that layer and the complete driving layer above, ending with the visible variables. The basic binary factors are logistic regressions; additional deterministic transformations or more expressive neural conditionals are optional. The recognition model proceeds bottom-up and can likewise be autoregressive within a layer, although the paper usually omits those recognition dependencies. Decoder ancestral sampling follows the top-down layer and within-layer orders and draws exact samples from the specified model; recognition sampling is exact for q but generally only approximate for the model posterior. Jointly train encoder and decoder toward the free-energy cost E_q[log q(h|x)-log p(x,h)], using the paper’s approximate gradient procedure through stochastic units. In Appendix A’s isolated Bernoulli calculation, with probability p depending on parameter theta and downstream f otherwise independent of theta, its final estimator is grad_theta(p) f-prime(h)/(2 q(h)), with h sampled from q. Its expectation equals grad_theta(p) times the average of the endpoint derivatives. This matches the finite-difference gradient for linear or quadratic f but need not for higher-order functions. The record distinguishes this approximation from the exact variational identity.

The generative and recognition parameters are separate, rather than tied symmetric connections of a Boltzmann machine. Related later variational autoencoders and deep belief networks are not treated as identity aliases. Wake-sleep is a training option, and its sleep recognition step is not generally the data-ELBO gradient. A shared variational motivation does not establish a single objective decreased by all model variants.

claims.statement: A top-down directed model p_theta(x,h) assigns probabilities to observed inputs and hidden configurations; a separately parameterized bottom-up model q_phi(h|x) produces a tractable approximate posterior. In the original layered binary construction, unit states in a layer are conditionally independent given the adjacent driving layer, with independent top-layer generative priors. Recognition proceeds through an acyclic bottom-up pass. The variational free energy is E_q[log q(h|x)-log p(x,h)], and log p(x) equals its negative plus KL(q(h|x)||p(h|x)); the negative free energy is therefore a lower bound under the normalized-model and support conditions. The paper describes stochastic recognition samples and, separately, a deterministic approximation that substitutes recognition means for sampled binary activities and neglects associated correlations. Its stochastic training alternative uses wake-sleep. The generative conditional need not be sigmoid: Appendix A considers noisy-or and other imaging rules. These choices do not change the defining presence of distinct generative and recognition models.
